neighbours.label: the verb right after a first-person singular subject 'I' ('I had', 'I was'), as against the same verb after he, she, we or they
fire:
The trip was planned months ago.
I had a long talk with the guide on the first morning.

Our office moved to a new building.
I was given a desk next to the window.

The festival lasted three days.
I had never seen so many people in one field.

The storm knocked out the power.
I was reading by candlelight until midnight.

The course started in September.
I had to buy four expensive textbooks.

The hospital was quiet that night.
I was on duty in the children's ward.

The match went to extra time.
I had almost lost my voice by the end.

The museum reopened after repairs.
I was among the first visitors to go in.
quiet:
The trip was planned months ago.
She had a long talk with the guide on the first morning.

Our office moved to a new building.
He was given a desk next to the window.

The festival lasted three days.
They had never seen so many people in one field.

The storm knocked out the power.
My father was reading by candlelight until midnight.

The course started in September.
The students had to buy four expensive textbooks.

The hospital was quiet that night.
A young nurse was on duty in the children's ward.

The match went to extra time.
The coach had almost lost his voice by the end.

The museum reopened after repairs.
Our class was among the first visitors to go in.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.8 on 'had'/'was' after 'I'; the same clauses with other subjects 0.0-0.2
notes: Card peaks: ' had' x11, ' was' x10, mostly 'I| had', 'I| was'. Probe: 'I had great fun' 0.728, 'I had a dentist appointment' 0.728, 'I was fortunate' 0.697, 'I was born' 0.697, "I'm very happy" 0.520; 'Last summer I had' only 0.337; 'She had great fun' 0.069, 'We had a wonderful time' 0.179, 'The weather had been' 0.004. Positivity does not matter; the subject does. Items start a new line after a lead sentence, as on the card.
